text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.2,"launches":1.2,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":0.6},"rationale":"Three attempts observed: attempt-00 (block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0) remains fastest at 157.29us, smem=32768, 2 blocks/SM. attempts-01/02 both selected block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256 with swizzle 16 then 64, simulated identically at 186.64us (same traffic 34.60MB, same blocks/SM=3); swizzle change produced no latency change, so the panel reuse proxy is not paying off here and small tiles/short block_K add launch overhead. Both compiled and passed numerics/SMT. Revision: drop block_M=16/32 and block_K=32 to stop re-selecting the losing small-tile regime, keeping block_M 64/128 and block_K 64/128 to test the untested larger-tile/deeper-K hypothesis; keep block_N up to 256 to probe fewer launches; stages 2-4 to explore overlap; threads 128/256 (256 worked, 128 untested for warp sensitivity). Swizzle trimmed to [0,4,8] since identical latency at 16/64 and M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows for block_M=64, so larger panels have no reuse headroom; avoid spending rounds on equivalent swizzles. Weights: footprint lowered to 0.6 (smem at cap but not the limiter), pipeline raised to 1.5 to favor stages=3-4 with block_K=64/128, traffic/launches each 1.2 as DRAM 34.6MB and block count dominate the observed ranking. Shared limit kept 32768 (hard portability cap binds). Next hypothesis: block_M=128/64 with block_N=128/256, block_K=64/128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256 to see if larger tiles with deeper K-pipelining beat 157.29us; validation scope note: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements."}
